status.basis: Revised Statutes sec. 4887: expired with Edison's Canadian patent No. 10,654 for the same invention, dated 1879-11-17, issued for 5 years and extended by fee for 10 more. The courts treated the Canadian term as one continuous 15 years and held that the U.S. patent ran to its end (Edison Electric Light Co. v. Perkins Electric Lamp Co., 42 F. 327, C.C.D. Conn. 1890; Edison Electric Light Co. v. United States Electric Lighting Co., 52 F. 300, 2d Cir. 1892). The British patent No. 4,576, dated 1879-11-10 but sealed after the U.S. grant, did not limit it (Edison Electric Light Co. v. Waring Electric Co., 59 F. 358, C.C.D. Conn. 1894); Bate Refrigerating Co. v. Sulzberger, 157 U.S. 1 (1895), held that a foreign patent issued before the U.S. grant limits the U.S. term. The appended Patent Office certificate of 1883-12-18 limiting the term was held void in 52 F. 300 and cancelled by the appended order of 1893-03-15; the statute applied without it. The 17-year date would have been 1897-01-27. No court states the exact day: 1894-11-17 ends the Canadian 15 years; Katznelson and Howells (2012) give 1894-11-19.
